reason: QA/qa-result.md is created by the first QA run, so it does not exist in a fresh install.
'usually' is a deliberate hedge in a role description; the rule is a style check.
<Service> and <tool> are placeholders in an example sentence, not XML.
A typographic apostrophe inside the text of a user-facing message, on purpose.

agnix's list of current tools has no MultiEdit, but older Claude Code versions have it; listing it keeps the researcher read-only there too, and a name Claude Code doesn't know in disallowedTools does nothing.

These allow the kit's own scripts so routine steps don't prompt. The guard still checks each call but not what a script does inside (tests/known-gaps.md), and in auto mode Claude Code drops the rules, which only adds prompts.
The body is just over the spec's 5000-token guide; the long reference parts already live in references/ and load only when needed.
morph-init's job is to write the project's own .claude/settings.json (the guard hook and permissions). It never reads the user's Claude Code config or credentials.
The flagged text is a question asking the owner whether to auto-approve edits and checks; the owner decides, and the guard's prompts and deny rules stay either way.
`npx vitest` is an example of a project's own test command in an allow rule, not an MCP server.
"with no warning" describes the output when there is no newer release; it is not an instruction to ignore safety checks.
